children: Methanex said it plans to exit the New Zealand natural gas industry, citing a continued decline in supply.

The Methanol producer on Tuesday said it agreed to sell substantially all of its natural gas contractual entitlements in the country as they expire through the end of the decade, beginning in the first quarter of next year.
It said it plans to indentifitely idle its New Zealand production facilities in the first quarter, while preserving the sites in case it decides to restart operations based on future circumstances.

"Given the continued decline in domestic natural gas availability and the lack of a clear pathway to meaningful new supply, Methanex has determined that continued operations in New Zealand are not sustainable and as such has taken steps to optimize value from its remaining New Zealand gas position," the company said.
The company said it does not expect to incur material cash costs from the move, adding that any updates to production or financial guidance will be included in its quarterly financial updates.
